title: Maximum Xor Product
summary: For integers a, b, and n, find the highest product of (a XOR x) * (b XOR x) for 0 <= x < 2^n, then return the result modulo 10^9 + 7.
statement: For integers a, b, and n, find the highest product of (a XOR x) * (b XOR x) for 0 <= x < 2^n, then return the result modulo 10^9 + 7. XOR denotes the bitwise exclusive OR operation.
constraints: Maximize (a XOR x)*(b XOR x) and return the product modulo 1,000,000,007.
reference_solution:
def maximum_xor_product(a,b,n):
    modulus=1_000_000_007;first=(a>>n)<<n;second=(b>>n)<<n
    for bit in range(n-1,-1,-1):
        left=a>>bit&1;right=b>>bit&1
        if left==right:first|=1<<bit;second|=1<<bit
        elif first>second:second|=1<<bit
        else:first|=1<<bit
    return first*second%modulus

hints: Equal source bits can be made one in both factors; differing bits must go to exactly one factor.
Preserve fixed high bits, then process controllable bits from high to low while balancing the factors.
Set both on equal bits; on differing bits give the one-bit to the currently smaller prefix.
For a fixed sum contribution at a differing bit, the product is largest when the two factors are as balanced as possible.

tests.explanation: The best low-bit choices produce factors fourteen and seven, whose product is 98.
Balancing the two XOR results yields the maximum product 930.
